newsitem.title: BERMUDA: ADT rejects Western Resources takeover bid as inadequate.
newsitem.headline: ADT rejects Western Resources takeover bid as inadequate.

text.p: ADT Ltd., the largest provider of electronic security services in North America and Britain, Wednesday rejected a $3.5 billion takeover bid by Western Resources Inc. as "inadequate."
Western Resources, which already owns 27 percent of ADT, spent much of 1996 laying the groundwork to take full control of ADT. It made its offer in December.
In a letter to shareholders, ADT said the "preliminary view" of its board of directors, based on the limited information presently available, is that the offer is inadequate.
ADT said it has scheduled a special general meeting of shareholders for July 8 and sent a notice of the meeting to shareholders.
ADT also said it expects to take a one-time charge of about $110 million after taxes and report a $50 million gain from the sale of its remaining interest in Limelight Plc.
The charge was for the integration of the security businesses that ADT acquired recently as part of Automated Security (Holdings) and for enhancing technological infrastructure.
ADT said the integration of the businesses into ADT should bring about "significant future cost savings."

ADT provides continuous monitoring of commercial and residential security systems to over 1.7 million customers. It is also the nation's second-largest provider of vehicle auction services, with 27 auction centres.
ADT's stock edged down 12.5 cents to $22.625, while Western Resources rose 25 cents to $31.25 on the New York Stock Exchange shortly before midday.
